prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. Quiet interior of a small nineteenth-century Lofoten fisherman’s cottage. A tired French naturalist in plain 1860s clothes at a rough table revises his loosely gathered manuscript, one hand resting on a page. Through the small square window there is grey Norwegian water and a jagged island silhouette. Fishing nets drying on a peg. The written marks are indistinct. No modern objects.
